I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My land is 8 mu of contracted farmland — that's what my family has. At my age, my son comes back during the busy planting and harvest times to help, but most of the year it's just me.

I don't need to think hard about what to grow. Everyone here grows wheat then maize — winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields. That's the rotation. The soil is right for it, the water is there (we have the village well), and I know how to do it. The seed shop in town stocks the seeds, and I can sell to the grain station. I've never grown vegetables or anything else — too complicated at my age, and I don't have the connections to sell them well.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved variety the seed shop has — they've been pushing 矮抗58 or something similar lately. Better than saving my own seed, which I used to do but the yields dropped. I'll put down compound fertilizer (磷酸二铵) when I till before planting, then urea in spring when the wheat is jointing. I'll water four times: the winter water (冬灌) before it freezes, then jointing, heading, and grain fill. I spray herbicide once in autumn when it's young, and if powdery mildew gets bad in spring, I'll spray again.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed —郑单958 or whatever they have. I plant right after wheat harvest in June. I apply compound fertilizer as base and throw urea on when it's knee-high. If July is dry I'll water once or twice. I spray once for corn borer if I see the damage.

I use rotary tillage. Ploughing is too hard on my body now, and rotary is fine.
